title: kiosk-developer-labs-and-failsafe-patterns-sketch
body:
Purpose
---
Quick note: this is a working sketch for a lightweight in-console "Developer Kiosk" — a micro-experience to let engineers (and non-engineers) explore Redwood SDKs and runtime behaviors in <5 minutes. Goal: reduce friction for first-time experiments, capture early telemetry, and teach predictable failure-recovery patterns.

Why a kiosk?
- Many quickstarts assume a local dev loop; but product demos, PMs, and Solution Engineers need a frictionless interactive demo inside Console.
- Lowering the mental load: ephemeral creds, guided scenarios, and an observable trace make it safe for non-core teams to experiment without creating infra noise.

Core features (MVP)
- Scenario chooser: Select small prebuilt flows ("hello-gen", "chat-fallback", "embeddings-search") with one-click run.
- Ephemeral API key: spins a scoped token valid 15m, auto-revoked.
- Inline code sandbox: small JS/py snippets editable and runnable against hosted endpoint.
- Failure simulator: toggle latency, token errors, 429s, and service fallbacks to see SDK retry behavior.
- Trace view: condensed request timeline, token counts, and a copyable curl/SDK snippet.
- Feedback hook: capture a short rating + note that links back to a triage board.

Operational guardrails
- Rate quota throttles tied to sandbox project.
- No data persistence by default; option to save a sample session with explicit consent.
- Audit trail: kiosk sessions attached to team account for 30d.

Acceptance criteria (short-term)
- New user can run a scenario and see generated text within 45s of clicking.
- Ephemeral key is issued and revoked automatically; session logs visible in Console.
- Failure simulator reproduces 429 and triggers documented SDK retry path (observable).
- Telemetry emitted: scenario_id, latency_ms, tokens_out, error_code; upstream ingestion tag set.

UX flow (happy path)
1) Console > Try SDK button -> opens modal with scenarios.
2) User selects "chat-fallback" -> a short explanation + expected outcomes.
3) Click Run -> ephemeral key shown + small code sandbox.
4) Run -> trace appears, streaming output.
5) Option to toggle "simulate 429" and re-run.
6) Short feedback prompt after run.

Developer notes / implementation sketch
- Frontend: small React micro-app embedded in Console, feature-flagged. Keep bundle < 150KB by using existing UI primitives.
- Backend: new /kiosk/sessions API that mints ephemeral keys (scoped to read-only generation endpoints) and emits events to ingestion pipeline.
- Telemetry schema: include kiosk_scenario, session_id, step, result_hash, token_count. Add a boolean field "simulated_failure".
- Security: ephemeral keys should not allow persistent storage calls or access to customer data. Use short-lived service principal.

Sample sandbox snippet (JS, minimal)
// replace KEY with ephemeral token
fetch('/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-lite', prompt: 'Summarize: a 2-sentence elevator pitch'})
})
.then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log).catch(console.error)

Open questions
- Do we provide a "record session" opt-in that stores prompt/response for future teaching packs? GDPR implications.
- How do we expose mobile SDK patterns? Could embed a GRPC-web example or short video clip.
- Ownership: who triages feedback? Proposed: DevExp + Solutions Eng rotation.

Next steps (next 2 sprints)
- Spike: prototype frontend modal + ephemeral key flow (owner: Marco) — 1 week.
- Telemetry hook + ingestion mapping (owner: Priya) — 1 sprint.
- Small user test with 6 non-dev internal users (owner: Leah) — collect qualitative notes.

Notes to self (scratch)
- Keep scenario library tiny: 4 scenarios max for MVP.
- Use existing sample models only (no new model onboarding).
- Tie feedback items to JIRA-ENG-1423.

References
- prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kiosk-prototypes/pull/12
- related ticket: JIRA-ENG-1423
- inspiration: internal on-site demo rig + Gist of ephemeral-keys pattern
